subject: ZenHealth POC kickoff — recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.inference>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-11-18T09:12:34-08:00
Subject: ZenHealth POC kickoff — recap & next steps

Hi Sara / Tom —

Thanks again for a productive kickoff this morning. Per our call, I wanted to capture the pain, goals, scope, success metrics and immediate next steps so we’re aligned heading into the POC. Please reply with any edits; otherwise we’ll consider this the working plan.

Summary of pain & goals
- Pain: Clinical intake notes are inconsistent, and existing triage automation misses 18–22% of social determinants triggers. This is increasing manual review and slowing patient intake.
- Goal: Improve automated extraction and triage precision to reduce manual review load by 40% and increase correct SDOH flagging recall to >=85% on the pilot set.

POC scope (4 weeks)
- Dataset: 10k de-identified intake notes (ZenHealth-labeled subset).
- Features: intent classification, entity extraction (SDoH categories), and a lightweight reranking step for triage priority.
- Deliverables: weekly eval reports, prompt/eval set, deployed Redwood inference endpoint + simple UI for reviewers, training for SRE/ops handoff.

Success metrics
- Primary: recall >=85% and precision >=75% on SDoH detection on the held-out eval set.
- Secondary: reduce reviewer time per case by 40% (measured via sampling) and tail latency P95 < 250ms for inference.

Owners & roles
- ZenHealth: Sara (POC sponsor), Tom (data/labeling owner), Security contact: security@zenhealth.com
- Redwood: Marissa (POC lead / PM), Aditya (solutions lead — data ingestion & infra), Rishi (runtime & performance).

Timeline & milestones
- Week 0 (this week): data access + SSO + transfer of 10k records (de-identified)
- Week 1: baseline eval on current model; initial prompt set + eval harness delivered
- Week 2: first deployed model + integration with UI for reviewer testing
- Week 3: iterate on prompt set & quantization profile; cost/latency tuning
- Week 4: final report + handoff / next steps (production plan or expansion).

Access / setup steps (action items)
1) ZenHealth: share S3 transfer credentials OR grant Redwoods-inference@zenhealth IAM role to a staging bucket. (Owner: Tom)
2) ZenHealth: confirm PII/PHI de-identification checklist and sign off (Owner: Sara; Security copy).
3) Redwood: create initial evaluation harness and share Drive folder with prompt set (Owner: Marissa).
4) Redwood: provision dedicated staging endpoint; Aditya to confirm access (Owner: Aditya).

Attachments: zenhealth-poc-scope.pdf (scope + sample prompt set) attached.

Next meeting:
- Proposed: Tue, Nov 23, 10:00 AM PST — data handoff + access verification (I’ll send calendar invite once we confirm).

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.
—
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference

Sara — thanks, good notes. Quick answers inline: 

> Data access: we prefer to grant an IAM role for the staging bucket rather than share long-lived creds. Tom will provision the role and share the ARN by EOD Tuesday.

Perfect — that works for us. Aditya: once Tom shares the role ARN, can your team validate the cross-account role and confirm we can mount the bucket to the staging environment?

> De-id checklist: I’ll run this past our privacy team; can we get a copy of Redwood’s de-id verification checklist to speed sign-off?

Attached is a short checklist and our recommended verification steps (also uploaded to the Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B_example_drive_link). We are also happy to walk your privacy team through the checklist in a 30-minute session.

> Security: our security team prefers all endpoints to be behind our VPN and to use SSO (Okta). Is that supported for the staging endpoint or do you need a short-term exception?

We support Okta SSO and can place the staging endpoint behind a VPN peering for the duration of the POC. There is one small caveat: if we need to use Redwood-managed monitoring dashboards (for SRE debugging) we'll request temporary read-only access from your network. We can minimize any exposure.

> SLA baseline for uptime and latency for the staging endpoint

For the dedicated staging pool we’ll target: 99.5% uptime and P95 latency <= 250ms (token generation; end-to-end latency will depend on request size). We’ll include these targets in the POC report and track them via the Console.

I’ve attached a quick setup checklist (zenhealth-poc-setup-checklist.xlsx) that lists all access items and owners; I’ll also create the HubSpot deal record and share the link (https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/987654321).

Next steps (owners):
- Tom: share IAM role ARN + confirm staging bucket by Tue EOD (owner: Tom)
- Sara: get privacy sign-off on de-id checklist (owner: Sara)
- Aditya: validate role & provision staging endpoint once role shared (owner: Aditya)
- Rishi: prepare baseline eval and perf harness by Friday

I’ll send the calendar invite for Nov 23 at 10:00 AM PST pending confirmation.


Marissa
